name: Energy Display
description: The battery-powered Energy Display, which shows the power, monthly cost and monthly energy of up to three iMeters, or of data a modem sends it, and the room temperature.

verification.note: The Energy Display Developer Notes label D9 through D13 as average kilowatt-hours, five bytes for a four-byte value; the catalog reads D9 through D12.

extendedCommands.name: readMeterIds
extendedCommands.description: Reads the IDs of the meters in groups 1 to 3.

extendedCommands.name: writeMeterId
extendedCommands.description: Sets the ID of the meter, or modem, in the group in D1. A modem linked this way receives the display's meter reads.

notes: When its Synchronize button is pressed, the display sends Get iMeter Status (cmd1 0x82, cmd2 0x00) to each linked meter or modem, then stays awake for 3 seconds. Programming it needs stay awake on (cmd2 0x06) within those 3 seconds. A modem answers with the iMeter's reply, CRC included.

Every 3 minutes the display checks the temperature; when it has changed by more than 1 degree Celsius, it broadcasts cmd1 0x6E to group 4 (flags 0x8F, To 00 00 04) with the temperature in half degrees Celsius in cmd2.
Here cmd1 0x2F with cmd2 0x01 reads and writes the meter in each group, not the ALL-Link database.
The Energy Display Developer Notes don't say whether the extended Sets carry a checksum.
